page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.large is a general-purpose, ninth-generation cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture. It delivers 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.3 GHz without hardware multithreading, coupled with 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache infrastructure includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. In addition to a 1 Gbps baseline network interface, this instance includes 118 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage, providing fast, low-latency disk access directly attached to the host.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded data compression capabilities, with gzip single-threaded compression reaching 36.33 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 17.2 GB/sec, placing both in the top tier of evaluated instances. Synthetic memory evaluations through PassMark yield a strong score of 2876.9, with uncached read throughput at 66.01 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core throughput reflects the small two-core profile: the multi-core stress-ng score of 4005.17 and PassMark CPU score of 2191.41 place it in the lower percentiles overall, and 7B parameter LLM inference achieves only 4.77 tokens per second.

The bundled NVMe storage and balanced memory configuration deliver solid resource efficiency for workloads requiring local scratch space without provisioning network storage. With static web serving throughput hitting 8.06 GB/sec, Redis SET performance at 6.51 million operations per second, and PassMark database operations scoring 4032.31, the m9gd.large is well aligned for lightweight caching tiers, web application hosting, build systems requiring temporary high-speed local disk, and containerized microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.large is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 architecture and AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 2 dedicated physical cores operating at 3.3 GHz, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 118 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 1 Gbps baseline networking. Compute benchmarks show exceptional single-core compression performance, registering 36.33 GB/sec in gzip testing, combined with a strong PassMark memory benchmark score of 2876.9. While limited to 2 cores for heavy multi-threaded processing, its balanced compute-to-memory ratio and fast internal storage make it well suited for lightweight database operations, Redis in-memory caches, static web serving, and transient data processing workloads.
